failure_summary.description: Agents chose a less direct endpoint or added overlapping or unrelated calls instead of limiting calls to distinct requested checks.
Agents serialized numeric values as numbers despite string-valued format examples, or placed parameters in the wrong group or shape.
Agents missed an explicit facet or altered a search target rather than preserving the requested subject.

patch.reasoning: The skill already covers coverage checklists and required-versus-optional grouping, so those rules need no duplication. These edits sharpen endpoint tie-breaking when tools overlap and clarify that call-format examples take precedence over schema types for serialization.

edits.target: Keep only calls that cover distinct requested results; reject speculative, duplicate, or adjacent calls, and candidates whose schemas cannot express the requested target without misusing fields or inventing arguments.
edits.content: When several endpoints appear to fit, choose the one whose documented operation most directly performs the requested check; a broad endpoint is suitable only when it fully covers the requested result. A request to use multiple tools does not justify multiple alternatives for the same facet—add a call only for a distinct requested result.

edits.target: Serialize values according to the required call-format convention: follow explicit examples that consistently encode values as strings, even for numeric or boolean parameters; otherwise follow the declared schema types.
edits.content: Serialize values according to the required call-format examples before falling back to schema types. If an applicable example encodes numeric or boolean-like values as strings, use strings for matching parameters even when the schema declares NUMBER or BOOLEAN; use native types only when no applicable format example establishes an encoding.
